title: Nomad's Delight
description: Bringing the hearty culinary traditions of the steppe nomads to your Farmer's Delight kitchen.
body:
![logo](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/7afd81ceb537b63c2a5b9532a0cb8cdb7e140bc8.png) ## Description A [Farmer's Delight]([https://modrinth.com/mod/farmers-delight]) addon that brings the rich, hearty culinary traditions of the Central Asian steppe nomads to your Minecraft kitchen. Embrace nomadic life with food built for the road: traditional dishes, ingredients, and storage solutions inspired by real steppe cuisine, reimagined for survival worlds. Saddle up, fire up the cooking pot, and taste the spirit of the steppes - As bolsyn! ## Features - 50+ new traditional and original dishes & ingredients - 19 new advancements to chase - Two new functional blocks: **Curd Bag** (Qaltasha), a portable storage pouch, and **Butter Churn**, a traditional churn (Qubi) used for processing dairy - Recipes and mechanics that hook directly into Farmer's Delight's cooking and farming systems

## Before You Download - Requires **Farmer's Delight** as a dependency - Currently available for **Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge** only - Fabric and additional Minecraft versions are planned for future releases ## About the Project This is our first modding project - we wanted to bring the food of our home on the steppe into Minecraft. Bug reports, balance suggestions, and feedback are very welcome on our [GitHub Issues page](https://github.com/DosyaKitarov/NomadsDelight/issues). ## Languages Currently, the mod supports Kazakh, English and Russian. We plan to add more languages over time, but we would honestly love to see the community lead this effort! If you want to translate the mod into your native language, please feel free to contribute. We truly prefer human translations because they preserve the actual cultural meaning, humor, and depth of the dishes, whereas our machine translations can feel a bit robotic and dry. ## Credits Created by [DosyaKitarov](https://github.com/DosyaKitarov) and [ninsent](https://github.com/ninsent).
